transcript: Lin-Manuel Miranda has a Broadway credit that we don't talk much about anymore but it might speak to some thorny issues that are still relevant today. welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history in 2009, a revival of West Side Story opened on Broadway directed by one of the show's writers, Arthur Laurents and while it was a traditional revival in most ways there was one big twist Laurent’s partner had reported seeing a Spanish-language production of West Side Story in Colombia and said that the dynamic shift made the Sharks feel more like the heroes of the story feeling inspired, Laurents decided to incorporate Spanish translations into the Broadway revival and Lin-Manuel Miranda hot off the success of In the Heights was hired to write the translations not just for sections of dialogue but for the lyrics as well. most notably the Sharks’ verses in the Tonight quintet and in the songs I Feel Pretty and A Boy Like That, the great Stephen Sondheim who of course wrote the original lyrics gave his blessing to Miranda with the one stipulation that the Spanish lyrics had to rhyme in all the same places. but audiences were not quite as thrilled with it. they did briefly try having English supertitles but ultimately decided against them. Then about 6 months into the Broadway run they decided to partially walk back some of these changes restoring most of the English lyrics to A Boy Like That and in a couple other small places. they found that a surprising portion of their audiences were not familiar with the show beforehand and so that moment just wasn't landing dramatically the way they wanted it to. in the same New York Times article they admitted that some of their investors were against the Spanish lyrics but said that was a “negligible factor” for the changes which to be fair, does make sense considering they were making a lot of money already at that point. full disclosure: when I started researching for this video i had a much more cynical narrative in my head when they say the change was artistically motivated, I kind of believe them because I think if they were truly motivated by cowardice they probably would have removed a lot more of the Spanish a lot sooner and I give him some credit for taking a risk like this in a community of musical theater fans who are notoriously puristic clinging to every word of their sacred canon for dear life and constantly resisting any opportunity to sit in the potential discomfort of something that they don't fully know or understand even when that's kind of the point of the show and don't get me wrong I have no doubt there was still some of that going on here but still people were showing up to the revival anyway. it got mostly positive reviews and got some award attention so all things considered the community didn't react that badly to it. but still i have a few critical thoughts: first of all, I’ve seen a decent amount of theatre in other languages, without English translations and i find that my ability to follow it depends a lot on the sharpness of the direction I’ve even seen a couple shows *with* English translations where I was following the show better just by watching the actors. I saw this revival on tour and I don't remember it very well so I can't really weigh in here but I suspect that the audience not understanding this number could have been more of a failure of direction second, I obviously don't think this production alone is to blame for the unfortunate realities of broadway audience demographics but it is significant to consider that the changes were supposedly made to accommodate audience members who were not yet familiar with the show. but who were these new audiences they were accommodating? clearly not Spanish-speakers despite this show being ostensibly about their experience. still though, knowing Broadway audiences I’m a little encouraged that they got away with it as much as they did and I’m encouraged by the success of a show like Buena Vista Social Club which also has a lot of un translated Spanish lyrics. But still a long way to go obviously so may we strive for a warmer welcome in all areas of our society
